image_description: A studio product shot displaying a collection of black loudspeakers arranged on a reflective white surface against a grey gradient background. The set includes two large tower-style speakers with dual drivers (woofer and tweeter), four smaller satellite speakers, and one center-channel speaker. All units feature black rectangular enclosures with silver/grey metallic-looking driver cones.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All visible speaker units clearly exhibit rigid, geometric box-like structures consistent with standard loudspeaker enclosures.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Each unit displays distinct circular driver elements. The larger units show size differentiation between the main woofer and the upper tweeter.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vertical arrangement of a larger lower driver and smaller upper driver is clearly visible on the tall tower speakers and the center channel unit.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The driver cones appear to have a smooth, metallic, or highly reflective plastic finish rather than the matte texture typical of paper or polypropylene. The 'rubber surround' detail is indistinct due to image resolution and lighting glare.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No grilles are present; the drivers are fully exposed ('naked' cone design).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The speakers are angled to show front and side profiles; the rear panels containing terminals are completely occluded from view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The enclosures have a uniform black finish consistent with painted MDF or plastic, which are standard materials for this class.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The speaker cones exhibit an unnatural, uniform metallic sheen that lacks the subtle textural grain of real paper/polypropylene cones. This suggests a material rendering error common in AI generation where 'shiny' is over-applied to curved surfaces.

artifact_observations.location: Base of the central floor-standing speaker
artifact_observations.reasoning: The base of the largest central speaker appears to merge slightly with the reflective surface. The shadow/reflection boundary is soft and ill-defined, making the physical footprint of the object ambiguous compared to the sharper bases of the surrounding satellite speakers.
The elliptical shape of the driver on the far-left speaker seems slightly inconsistent with the viewing angle established by the other speakers, appearing somewhat flattened or warped.

selected_experts.reason: To verify if the specific configuration of drivers and enclosure shapes aligns with known commercial loudspeaker designs or if they represent hallucinated geometries.
To analyze the contact shadows and reflections on the white surface, ensuring each speaker sits physically on the plane and does not float or merge into the background.
To check for edge bleeding between the black cabinets and the grey/white background, and to ensure the circular drivers are perfectly contained within the front baffles without melting.
To assess the realism of the lighting reflections on the metallic-looking cones and the consistency of the studio lighting environment.

focus_areas: Material realism of driver cones (metallic vs paper texture)
Physical grounding and shadow consistency of the central tower speaker
Geometric symmetry of circular drivers across different viewing angles
Edge sharpness between black enclosures and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'metallic' appearance of the speaker cones. Real hi-fi speakers rarely have such uniformly shiny, mirror-like cones unless they are specific metal-dome tweeters, but here even the woofers look metallic. Investigate if this is a style choice or a texture generation artifact. Also, verify the base of the central speaker for 'floating' artifacts.
